identity_anchor.summary: ElizaOS is an MIT-licensed open-source repository on GitHub with its own documentation site.

evidence.claim: The elizaOS/eliza repository describes itself as an open source agentic operating system under the MIT license.
ElizaOS publishes its documentation index at docs.elizaos.ai.

memory_custody.summary: Per its docs, the framework stores agent memory (text, embeddings, metadata, relationships) in a database chosen by whoever runs the agent: embedded PGLite on the local filesystem by default, or PostgreSQL when POSTGRES_URL is set. A REST endpoint retrieves all memories for an agent, but no backup or export procedure is documented.

evidence.claim: Memories are persisted through the IDatabaseAdapter, which supports PGLite and PostgreSQL, storing full text, embeddings, metadata and relationships.
PGLite stores data in the local filesystem and defaults to ./.eliza/.elizadb; setting POSTGRES_URL selects PostgreSQL; the docs do not address backup or export.
GET /api/memory/{agentId}/memories retrieves all memories for a specific agent.

persistence_ops.summary: The main repository has commits dated November 5 and 6, 2026. Development continued after the foundation wound down in August 2026.

evidence.claim: The develop branch shows commits on November 5 and November 6, 2026.

economic_rails.summary: ElizaOS Cloud deploys agents to dedicated instances against account credits. The project's docs do not describe a project wallet or treasury.

evidence.claim: Cloud deployment runs on a dedicated EC2 instance, and troubleshooting asks users to verify they have credits in their account.

governance.summary: The code is public under the MIT license and changes land through public pull requests on GitHub. No formal decision process beyond the maintainers' repository control is documented. Press reported in August 2026 that the foundation behind the project was winding down after a legal settlement, with development to continue under its founder; the project's own pages do not say so.

evidence.claim: The repository is public and MIT-licensed.
Recent commits on develop are merged pull requests in the elizaOS organization.
Reported in press, not in the platform's own pages: the foundation began winding down after a legal settlement, and development of ElizaOS will continue (crypto.news, 5 August 2026).

recovery.summary: The docs advise operators to implement their own backup strategy for the agent database and give no restore procedure. The project keeps shipping, with commits on 5 and 6 November 2026. No incident or restart record is published in the project's own pages.

evidence.claim: The database adapter docs advise implementing proper backup strategies and give no restore procedure.
The develop branch shows commits on November 5 and 6, 2026.
